skill.name: fingerprint-ci-gate
skill.description: Gate a build on browser fingerprint regressions with liarjs - save a baseline scan as JSON, diff later runs against it, and fail the job when the consistency score falls below a floor. Use when asked to add a fingerprint or headless-detection check to GitHub Actions, GitLab CI or another pipeline, to catch a regression in a Chromium build or scraping harness before it ships, or to track how a fingerprint score changes across commits.
skill.summary: Run repeatable liarjs fingerprint scans, compare them with a baseline, and fail CI when defined checks regress.
skill.author: liarjsdev

security_audit.summary: The reviewed files describe a CI workflow for running version-pinned liarjs browser scans, storing results, and comparing them with a baseline. Static alerts are false positives for documented shell examples, CI commands, browser shared-memory configuration, and an explicitly disclosed network endpoint; the unintegrity-pinned npx dependency remains a supply-chain risk.

remediation.issue: CI examples resolve liarjs with the mutable semver specifier `liarjs@0.3`.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an exact package version and verify its lockfile or package-integrity hash before executing it in CI.

remediation.issue: The default scan endpoint sends cross-layer checks to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Use `--offline` for isolated builds or configure `--endpoint` to an organization-controlled deployment after reviewing data and retention.

remediation.issue: The Docker recipe mounts the workspace into the container.
remediation.suggestion: Use a minimal read-only workspace mount when possible and keep CI credentials unavailable to the scan process.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable CI Dependency Resolution
semantic_findings.description: The CI examples invoke `npx liarjs@0.3`, which permits registry resolution to change within the version range. A compromised or unexpected release could execute in the CI runner.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands use a non-exact npm version selector in CI, and the surrounding text treats that selector as the recommended pin. This creates a concrete supply-chain exposure even though the skill has no evident malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Browser fingerprint changes can reach production unnoticed and weaken automation reliability. This skill adds repeatable liarjs scans, baseline comparisons, and score-based CI failures.
actual_capabilities: Generate a JSON fingerprint scan with liarjs in headless mode.
Fail a pipeline when the scan score falls below a configured minimum.
Compare a current scan with a committed baseline and report changed checks.
Provide GitHub Actions and GitLab CI command examples.
Provide Docker and Playwright integration recipes.
Recommend offline scans or a self-hosted endpoint for network control.
limitations: It documents CI commands and does not run scans or modify pipeline files automatically.
Fingerprint scores vary with browser versions, execution mode, network conditions, and runner configuration.
The examples require Node 22 or newer and an available Chromium-compatible browser.
It does not determine whether a fingerprint change is harmful to a specific application.

use_cases.title: Protect Browser Automation Builds
use_cases.description: Add a repeatable fingerprint gate to a scraping or browser automation pipeline before merging Chromium or harness changes.

use_cases.title: Track CI Fingerprint Drift
use_cases.description: Commit a known-good baseline, compare later scans, and review changed checks in pull requests or pipeline artifacts.

use_cases.title: Validate a Playwright Harness
use_cases.description: Run checks inside an existing Playwright or Puppeteer suite and assert on individual failing check identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a basic liarjs fingerprint gate to my CI pipeline. Use headless mode, a minimum score of 60, and save the scan result as an artifact.

prompt_templates.title: Add Baseline Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI workflow that compares `baseline.json` with the current liarjs scan. Include clear exit-code handling and steps for reviewing changed checks.

prompt_templates.title: Containerize the Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Docker-based fingerprint scan for Node 22 and Chromium. Keep the browser sandbox enabled, configure shared memory, and run as a non-root user.

prompt_templates.title: Harden the Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this fingerprint CI design for reproducibility and security. Recommend exact dependency pinning, baseline governance, artifact handling, offline mode, and a self-hosted endpoint where appropriate.

best_practices: Use the same browser mode and runner conditions when creating and comparing baselines.
Pin the scanner version exactly and review baseline refreshes in separate commits.
Store failed scan artifacts and inspect individual check identifiers before changing thresholds.
anti_patterns: Do not lower the global score floor to hide checks that are always unsuitable for your environment.
Do not refresh a baseline without recording why the fingerprint changed.
Do not disable the Chromium sandbox or expose CI credentials to the scan process.

faq.question: What does this skill gate?
faq.answer: It gates CI on liarjs fingerprint scores or changes between a saved baseline and a current scan.

faq.question: Which environments are covered?
faq.answer: The recipes cover GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Docker, Playwright, and Puppeteer workflows.

faq.question: What does the minimum score do?
faq.answer: The scan exits with code 1 when its score is below the configured minimum, allowing CI to fail.

faq.question: Why use a baseline diff?
faq.answer: A baseline diff highlights checks that moved, which avoids treating stable environment-specific failures as new regressions.

faq.question: Can scans avoid outbound requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented offline mode skips cross-layer checks and makes no outbound request.

faq.question: What must the runner provide?
faq.answer: Use Node 22 or newer, a Chromium-compatible browser, enough shared memory, and the capabilities required by the browser sandbox.
